messages:
arya (AE): Heads-up — Large finance prospect (SafeHarbor) wants an on-prem POC in an air-gapped lab. They asked for packaging options, upgrade cadence commitments, and a one-page operator checklist they can hand to their infra team. Need to know what we can promise for no-egress installs.

nate (Solutions Eng): Quick Q: will the POC include the web console or just inference endpoints? Also do they require certified FIPS crypto and HSM integration?

arya (AE): Inference endpoints only for the POC. Security team asked for FIPS compatibility; they have a local HSM available.

ravi (Platform Eng): OK — we can deliver two artifact types for air-gapped: (A) offline container bundle (tar of images + signed manifest + installer) and (B) VM appliance image (qcow2/ova). For offline activation we support pre-signed license files that the operator drops in /var/lib/redwood/license.json — no phone-home.

morgan (Security): From compliance side: we will provide SBOM (CycloneDX), signed artifacts (Ed25519), and an example PKCS#11 integration for local HSMs. Telemetry: offline mode = telemetry disabled by default, and we can ship with telemetry binaries removed if required.

nate (Solutions Eng): Runtime notes: full runtime + base model shard ~10-14GB. Quantized variant can be ~3-6GB depending on model. Disk layout: /opt/redwood (bin, models, data), we recommend 60GB free to allow for deltas and logs.

ravi (Platform Eng): Upgrade story: we support reversible delta patches for runtime and model diffs. Recommended cadence: security hotfixes within 72 hours of release, minor patches monthly, model improvements quarterly. For customers with quarterly change windows we can stage rollout jobs (canary -> health check -> full). Installer supports dry-run: `./install.sh --dry-run --target /opt/redwood`. Rollback: supported, we keep three previous versions by default.

arya (AE): They have strict change-control windows (once per quarter) — that should be fine. Can we produce a one-page checklist that lists kernel constraints, ports, required modules, and verification steps?

nate (Solutions Eng): Yes. Checklist items I plan to include: minimum kernel 5.4+, required kernel modules (overlay, br_netfilter), required inbound ports (8080 for API; 8443 only if console included), recommended ulimits, GPU requirements per model profile (if GPU present), disk/ram guidance, offline signature verification steps.

morgan (Security): Add verification samples. Example verification steps for operators:

```
# verify checksum
sha256sum -c redwood-offline-bundle.tar.gz.sha256
# verify signature (Ed25519)
ed25519verify vendor_pub.ed25519 redwood-offline-bundle.tar.gz
```

morgan (Security): Also add: we can issue artifacts signed with FIPS-approved algorithms and provide guidance for validating with OpenSSL if required.

arya (AE): Good. Legal asked about SLA language for upgrades: can we commit to quarterly model updates and guarantee emergency security patch availability within 72 hours?

ravi (Platform Eng): That's our standard POC commitment: quarterly model refreshes included; emergency signed offline patches delivered within 72 hours of vulnerability triage. We should avoid promising automatic installs — we provide signed patches and operator-run update steps to respect change control.

arya (AE): FinOps also wants rough sizes for network-free delivery so they can prepare storage. Can you include both full and quantized sizes in the checklist?

nate (Solutions Eng): I'll include typical sizes: full runtime+model ~12GB, quantized variant ~4GB, plus 1-5GB for logs and tooling. For delta patches expect 50-300MB depending on change.

artifact-bot: Published artifact: redwood-offline-bundle-2026.12.01-rc1 (sha256: b2c9...4f1)

arya (AE): Timeline: they want the checklist + a signed sample license by Thursday so they can kick off review before Friday's change board. Can we meet that?

nate (Solutions Eng): I can draft the one-pager and sample operator commands by Thursday EOD. ravi, can you produce a sample signed license with allowed model list and expiry?

ravi (Platform Eng): Yes, will promote the RC1 bundle and sign a sample license. Need to confirm which model family they want included (base or quantized). Also need GPU info if they plan GPU-backed inference — kernel selection differs for A10 vs A100.

arya (AE): I'll ask the customer for model preference and whether they plan to use GPU in the lab. Also confirm HSM details for the license flow.

morgan (Security): I'll paste canned answers for typical security questionnaire items into the checklist (phone-home, data collection, SBOM availability, key management).

arya (AE): Great. Action items: nate -> one-page checklist + operator commands (Thu), ravi -> promote bundle + sample signed license (Thu), morgan -> canned questionnaire responses into the checklist (Thu). I'll update once customer confirms model/GPU. Thanks all :rocket:

artifact-bot: Signed artifact uploaded to internal store: https://artifacts.internal/offline/redwood-offline-bundle-2026.12.01-rc1.tar.gz.sig
notes: POC - air-gapped packaging and upgrade cadence discussion
